title: Symptom Burden by Level of Therapeutic Intensity in a Palliative Care Unit
official: Prevalence of Symptoms According to the Level of Diagnostic and Therapeutic Intervention in Patients Hospitalized in a Palliative Care Unit
summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how symptom burden differs according to the level of diagnostic and therapeutic intensity agreed for each patient, in adults with cancer admitted to a palliative care unit. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the symptom burden, measured with the Edmonton Symptom Assessment System (ESAS), of patients in each level of diagnostic and therapeutic intensity?
* Is the level of diagnostic and therapeutic intensity associated with overall symptom burden and with the frequency and intensity of each symptom? Participants will have their symptoms (such as pain, tiredness, nausea, or shortness of breath) and their level of diagnostic and therapeutic intensity assessed within the first 72 hours of admission, as part of routine care. The study does not change their treatment, and additional information will be collected from their medical records.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 18 years or older
* Admitted to the palliative care unit during the study period
* Underlying cancer related to the reason for admission
* Legal capacity to give informed consent or, failing that, availability of a legal representative
* Signed informed consent from the patient or the patient's legal representative

Exclusion Criteria:

* No diagnosis of underlying cancer
* Repeat admissions of the same patient during the study period (only the first admission will be included)
